metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (pricing.cpp) with a deployable entry point (main()), Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections or writes detected; the single CGI endpoint performs a read-only file lookup and returns pricing data. No user-specific state, no write operations. Classified as stateless-utility.

findings.title: Managed Compute — containerized but no managed orchestration provisioned
findings.description: The application has been containerized (Dockerfile using GCC 12 builder stage, httpd:2.4-alpine runtime) with Kubernetes deployment manifests targeting EKS. However, no IaC provisions managed compute infrastructure (EKS cluster, ECS service, Fargate, or Lambda).
findings.gap: Containerization is complete but no AWS managed compute provisioning exists in the repository.
findings.recommendation: Provision an EKS cluster (or ECS/Fargate) via IaC (CDK or Terraform) and deploy the existing k8s manifests. Alternatively, evaluate AWS Lambda for this stateless pricing function.

findings.title: Network Security — no network security configuration
findings.description: No network security configuration exists in the repository. No Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, no VPC definitions, no security groups. The k8s Service is ClusterIP but no explicit network isolation rules are defined.
findings.gap: Complete absence of network security configuration.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress/egress. When provisioning EKS via IaC, define private subnets with least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no managed API gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. The k8s Service exposes the CGI endpoint directly. A commented-out ALB Ingress Controller example exists but is not implemented.
findings.gap: No managed API entry point providing throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an AWS ALB Ingress Controller or API Gateway in front of the service with throttling and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — static capacity with no scaling
findings.description: The k8s Deployment uses static replicas: 2 with no Horizontal Pod Autoscaler configured.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — capacity is statically provisioned.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes HPA targeting CPU utilization or request rate.

findings.title: High Availability — no multi-AZ configuration
findings.description: The k8s Deployment has 2 replicas but no pod anti-affinity rules, no topology spread constraints, and no explicit multi-AZ configuration.
findings.gap: No multi-AZ fault isolation guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints or pod anti-affinity rules to spread replicas across AZs.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — partial IaC
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests define the application deployment surface but no IaC provisions the underlying infrastructure (EKS cluster, VPC, IAM roles).
findings.gap: Partial IaC coverage — application deployment in k8s manifests but AWS infrastructure not in code.
findings.recommendation: Add Terraform or CDK to provision EKS cluster, VPC, subnets, security groups, and IAM roles.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline, manual scp deployment
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline definitions found. The Makefile install target deploys via scp to a remote host.
findings.gap: Complete absence of CI/CD automation. All deployments are manual.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline with stages for: build Docker image, run tests, push to ECR, deploy to EKS.

findings.title: Programming Languages — pre-C++11 with no cloud-native tooling
findings.description: C++ (pre-C++11 style) using C-style functions (strcpy, strtok, sscanf, printf). No modern C++ features, no frameworks, no AWS SDK. CGI execution model is obsolete.
findings.gap: Language/framework combination has limited cloud-native tooling depth. Known security vulnerabilities (buffer overflows).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a cloud-native language with first-class AWS SDK support (Python, Go, Node.js/TypeScript, or Java/Kotlin).

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — tightly-coupled single-file binary
findings.description: Single 70-line C++ file containing all logic: CGI query parsing, file-based data lookup, HTML response rendering. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. Cannot be independently scaled, tested, or evolved.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as a modern microservice with clear separation: HTTP handler, pricing domain logic, and data access layer.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — no versioning
findings.description: No API versioning. The endpoint is /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi with no version prefix or headers.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy — breaking changes would affect all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: When rewriting, implement URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/pricing) from the start.

findings.title: Service Discovery — basic k8s DNS only
findings.description: The Kubernetes Service provides basic DNS-based discovery within the cluster. No service mesh, no API catalog, no explicit service registry.
findings.gap: Basic k8s DNS discovery only. No service mesh or API catalog.
findings.recommendation: For a single service this is adequate. As the system grows, consider AWS Cloud Map or a service mesh.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — flat file on local filesystem
findings.description: Pricing data stored as a pipe-delimited flat file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) on the local filesystem. No S3, no managed storage, no parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Data on local file system with no durability, versioning, access control, or cross-service accessibility.
findings.recommendation: Migrate pricing data to S3 with versioning or DynamoDB for low-latency key-value lookups.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — no abstraction pattern
findings.description: The lookup_price() function is the single data access point but is not a deliberate architectural pattern — no abstraction, no interface contract, hardcoded file path.
findings.gap: No deliberate data access layer pattern. File path hardcoded. No abstraction for swapping data source.
findings.recommendation: When rewriting, implement a repository pattern with an interface that abstracts the data source.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL — no database, flat file with no lifecycle
findings.description: No database engine exists. Data stored in hand-edited flat text file with no version management, no schema, no lifecycle management.
findings.gap: No structured data management. Flat file format has no schema evolution, validation, or version tracking.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a managed database (DynamoDB or RDS PostgreSQL) with schema and version management.

findings.title: API Authentication — no authentication on endpoints
findings.description: No API authentication of any kind. The CGI endpoint accepts any request without credentials.
findings.gap: Completely open API — no authentication, authorization, or request attribution.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication via API Gateway authorizer (JWT/Cognito) when exposing externally. For internal traffic, consider service mesh mTLS.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — no IdP integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. The application has no authentication at all, let alone centralized IdP integration.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration. No SSO, no federated auth.
findings.recommendation: When adding authentication, integrate with a centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or organization IdP).

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — good hardening but no scanning
findings.description: Alpine-based image with security context (runAsNonRoot, no privilege escalation, drop ALL capabilities). No patching automation or vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: Good container hardening but no automated patching or vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Add container image scanning (ECR, Trivy) in CI/CD. Configure Dependabot or Renovate for base image updates.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. Known vulnerabilities exist in source (buffer overflows, reflected XSS).
findings.gap: Complete absence of security scanning. Known vulnerabilities undetected by automated tools.
findings.recommendation: Add SAST (Semgrep, CodeGuru), container image scanning (Trivy, ECR), and dependency scanning in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no tracing instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No observability into request flows.
findings.recommendation: When rewriting, instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK. For current container, consider OTel sidecar.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — no SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions, no CloudWatch alarms, no latency targets, no error rate thresholds.
findings.gap: No formal service level objectives.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: availability (99.9%), latency p99 (<100ms), error rate (<0.1%). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No CloudWatch PutMetricData, no Prometheus metrics endpoint.
findings.gap: No visibility into business outcomes or service behavior.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom metrics: pricing lookup count by SKU, invalid SKU rate, response latency histogram.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — no alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — service failures go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for HTTP 5xx error rate, response latency p99, container restart count.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — rolling update only
findings.description: K8s Deployment defaults to RollingUpdate with readiness/liveness probes. No canary, no blue/green, no traffic shifting.
findings.gap: Default rolling update only — no staged validation of new versions.
findings.recommendation: Add Argo Rollouts or Flagger for canary deployments with traffic shifting.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states: 'No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output.'
findings.gap: Complete absence of automated testing. No regression safety net.
findings.recommendation: Add integration tests verifying: valid SKU pricing, invalid SKU handling, quantity multiplication, malformed input safety.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — no runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing patterns.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for: container crash loops, high error rates, pricing data corruption. Automate common remediations.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no ownership defined
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS for monitoring, no team-attributed alarms, no dashboards.
findings.gap: No observability infrastructure and no ownership model.
findings.recommendation: When implementing observability, define ownership via CODEOWNERS and team-tagged alarms.
